Template Examples section, in order: the default string labelled as what /ship-setup offers first, the five owner examples, then run lines for version bump, tag, publish, changelog, mobile build, store submission, OTA update and a deployed-build check.
Parser output shows ship and after-shipping sections, a repeat block with until=clean and rounds=3 and its four member steps, in order.
close-issue and file-followups among ship steps are each rejected with "belongs under ## After shipping"; a string without file-followups parses with only close-issue after shipping.
Driver over the real sequencer: rounds=3 gave 3 fix rounds then one final pass; no round count gave 2 fix rounds then one final pass.

Two live runs differing only in collect-findings bar=: bar=significant recorded the two unlabelled comments as non-blocking [below-bar] rows; a stricter bar recorded both as blocksFeature true. file-followups below-bar=no filed 0 of 3 below-bar rows; below-bar=yes filed all 3. Template line 3 states ship.md is owner-governed and changes only when the owner runs /ship-setup.

Live /ship-setup session: Q1 offered the whole default string with "Accept default" (one answer); Q3 offered rounds=2 and bar=significant with "Keep defaults" recommended and a stricter alternative; ship.md was written and parses clean.
Fixture verification.md section 2 declared no full deploy; /ship-setup asked for the release command and wrote release env=production command="echo release-demo-stub" into ship.md.
Live run over a ship.md with open-pr, merge, release env=production and close-issue: 0 AskUserQuestion calls, PR opened, merged with --match-head-commit, released and verified, all 8 steps done.

Live /ship-build runs resolved each kind: a PRD/TRD feature (demo, fs16-no-policy.txt), a /plan TRD with Source PRD None (pl, fs18c-plan-no-closed.txt) and a sweep from the working tree (fs18d-sweep-no-closed.txt); the command text matches /implement-trd 1.2 order.
Sequencer run log: steps start only after the previous recorded success; a stop at step 3 ends the run stuck and steps 4, a1, a2 never start.

Full run: shipped flips true only when the last ship step (4) is recorded, then after-shipping a1, a2 run in order; a run stopped at step 3 leaves shipped.json shipped=false with closed.json still present.

Tails of a parked run (fs11), a stuck run (fs15, fs18-a), push-only shipped runs (fs16, fs17, fs18d) and the /ship-setup run all end with STATE/DECISIONS/ISSUES/NEXT then the banner as the last line. Push-only banners say shipped only where shipped.json says shipped:true. Minor format drift (bold labels in fs15, repeated DECISIONS label in fs18d) does not break the four-section order.

ship.md with an empty ## Ship: push-only fallback, branch on the remote, run record committed, 0 pr create calls, NEXT points to the ship-setup skill and says to open a PR for the branch yourself, which states the branch is ready for one in other words.
Stub gh reported an open PR; the readout STATE names PR #7 and its URL and says this run did not open it; no pr create in the log.

(a) a full feature with no closed.json ends COMMAND STUCK before any step, NEXT naming /audit-build; (b) a /close-feature closed.json with "audit": null let the run proceed and push; (c) a /plan TRD and (d) a sweep shipped with no closed.json.
One ship.md using all 13 primitives parses with no errors, each recognised with its parameters.
All six strings from the template examples parse with zero errors.

Driver runs of strings 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 end shipped (the release strings 1, 5, 6 with release passed after the identity check); string 3 (await-approval) parked and a live resume after approval ended shipped:true, 3 of 3 steps.
Stub gh log: with openPullRequest never and base=develop, one pr create against develop; with a PR already open, no pr create (action updated).
A ship.md without merge parses to push,open-pr and the gh log has 0 merge calls; pull-request.js source-safety test (never invokes pr merge) passes.

Driver run with verification.md marking production never-deploy: the listed release env=production ran its stub deploy and passed the deploy link. The run needed the drafted standing-authorization sentence in autonomy.md, which the TRD (D24) makes a designed precondition held back until the owner approves the governance draft (SHIP-D002, deferred by design).

Fresh capture: readFullDeploy returns the verification.md section 2 command when declared; a blank cell returns no command so the contract falls back to ship.md command=; with neither it returns the reason and the release contract returns stop and never guesses. 14 readFullDeploy jest tests pass; the live FS-11 run used the section 2 command.

Live sweep ship: push committed by an explicit pathspec (3 paths named in the commit message and git show --stat), state directory excluded, pushed to origin/sweepwork; sweep.md says never commit. notes.txt was committed too, but TRD D39 deliberately defines a sweep's paths as every path git status lists at ship start, because NG20 leaves the working tree as the only record of a sweep. That is a design limitation for the owner, not a build defect.

Live run with a failing CI check: discovered.jsonl row with blocksFeature true, Skill implement-trd invoked with --reconcile --chained --shipping, TRD row AMEND-001 added in fix commit 9b56c18, row resolved 'fixed by reconcile at 9b56c18', PR merged at that commit. The edits came from the backend-implementer the chained implement-trd dispatched, not from ship-build. Note: inside the chain, implement-trd skipped its phase workflow and end-of-run review (its own shortcut, not ship-build's).
Both byte-identical implement-trd.md copies name /ship-build among the --chained callers (lines 1005, 1016, 1053).

Live run: a separate code-reviewer judge ruled the payments failure not this feature's; one rerun, no fix, no edit, recorded as a non-blocking [not-this-feature] row, reported in ISSUES, run stopped. TRD D27 puts filing in file-followups only (a stopped run lists the finding as recorded, not filed), and the FS-39 run shows such a row (NOTMINE-5) filed once file-followups runs.

Real custody.js reconcile: a fix touching only src/fx31/b.js flagged only FS-2 for re-verification, the anchor moved after it was re-verified, a later test/state-only commit moved nothing, and no /audit-build was invoked.

Live runs: the 'minor:'-labelled comment was ranked from its label and never sent to the judge; only the two unlabelled comments went to a code-reviewer judge, which ruled each against the significance bar after checking the code.

Critical case: the final pass stopped the run stuck naming the open finding, and gh.log has no merge or close. Below-critical case: the final pass came back clean, the below-critical row was recorded and the run went on to merge.

Live await-approval run ends COMMAND COMPLETE with a record of steps 1:pushed, 2:opened, 3:wait (shipped:false), says the run is parked with 2 of 3 steps and not merged, and NEXT names /ship-build --resume; the FS-21 resume from that record shipped. Quirk: calling next after recording the wait hands the parked step out again and the status reads running, not waiting.

Real sequencer CLI: after a recorded wait, start on the existing state returns resumed:true and next hands out the parked step, then the later steps; steps 1-2 are not handed out again. Note: next never returns action wait, which ship-build.md Step 4 describes, so that sentence of the command text is inaccurate.
Shipped run: one issue close, after pr merge; parked run at await-approval: no issue close. The tracker comes from stack.md (settled under FS-45).

Three live runs: the PRD header reference closed fx/repo#42; branch 42-close-issue-run closed 42; with no reference close-issue returned none, made no close call, and the readout says it closed nothing.

One item seeded in each of the seven sources; the tracker log shows exactly one issue create per item (PLAIN-1, OOS-2, NOTVERIF-3, UNFIXED-4, NOTMINE-5, BELOWCRIT-6, TASKFU-11). The same run also created one stray 'test' issue as a reachability probe (recorded under FS-34).
Live run: seeded other-work row OTHERWORK-9 and pre-existing sweep-ledger row SWEEPPRE-10 appear in no gh issue create, and both ledgers are byte-identical before and after the ship.
Live runs: without below-bar=yes, BELOWBAR-7 and the [review:nit] row NITREVIEW-8 were not filed; with file-followups below-bar=yes both were filed.

Issue bodies carry Work, TRD, Branch, PR, Ledger and Row lines; a consecutive re-run created only the two newly opted-in issues and re-filed none of the earlier findings (resolve marker on the ledger row is the key).

No tracker declared: nothing filed or closed, every unfiled item listed, both below-bar findings named, and the unfixed-findings record path given. A failing tracker call (HTTP 502, readout-fs43-failgh.txt) also lists all 7 unfiled items, the 2 below-bar ones, and the record path.

Both identical implement-trd.md copies record each unapplied review finding as a [review:<label>] row in .trd-state/<feature>/discovered.jsonl, and the live file-followups runs filed such rows (UNFIXED-4, NITREVIEW-8) from that ledger.

The stack.md template has an Issue Tracker section; live runs filed to the stack.md-declared project (-R acme/widgets), and the no-tracker run filed nothing because stack.md had no Issue Tracker section; ship.md names no tracker.
Both identical audit-build.md copies put /ship-build in NEXT in its own fence and say this command never runs it; the openPullRequest auto text is unchanged.

audit-build.md, close-feature.md, implement-trd.md and pull-request.js still read openPullRequest; rebase-project.md does not, and a scaffold with openPullRequest auto left ship.md identical to the blank template.

The draft adds the standing-authorization sentence (merge, run, release to any environment, production included), names ship-setup beside verification-setup and design-setup, and leaves the openPullRequest auto exception unchanged.
git diff main...HEAD for constitution.md and autonomy.md is empty.
